By default a test stops at its **first** failed keyword — everything after it is
skipped. Often that is what you want. But sometimes you want to check several
things and see **every** problem in one run: a form with many fields, a config
with many settings, a page with many elements.

The `robot:continue-on-failure` tag keeps a test running past failures and
reports them all together. (The `Run Keyword And Continue On Failure` keyword
does the same for a single step.)

## Task 1 — Report every problem at once

**Goal:** create `checks/audit.robot` with a test tagged
`robot:continue-on-failure` that makes several assertions — more than one of them
failing — so the run reports all the failures, not just the first.

Here is the same idea with different assertions. Adapt it so at least two checks
fail.

<!-- example -->
```robotframework
*** Test Cases ***
Config Check Reports All
    [Tags]    robot:continue-on-failure
    Should Be Equal    on    on
    Should Be Equal    yes    no
    Should Be Equal    1    2
```
<!-- /example -->

**Check:** the test `Audit Reports Every Problem` reports more than one failure.

<!-- hint -->
Tag the test so it keeps going: `[Tags]    robot:continue-on-failure`.
<!-- /hint -->
<!-- hint -->
Make several assertions with more than one wrong, e.g.
`Should Be Equal    left    right` and `Should Be Equal    up    down` — both are
reported, not just the first.
<!-- /hint -->
<!-- solution -->
```robotframework
*** Test Cases ***
Audit Reports Every Problem
    [Tags]    robot:continue-on-failure
    Should Be Equal    ${1}    ${1}
    Should Be Equal    left    right
    Should Be Equal    up    down
```
<!-- /solution -->

## Task 2 — Run it and read the combined failure

Run it:

```bash
uv run robot checks/audit.robot
```

The test fails once, but the message collects **every** failed check:

```terminal
$ uv run robot checks/audit.robot
==============================================================================
Audit
==============================================================================
Audit Reports Every Problem                                           | FAIL |
Several failures occurred:

1) left != right

2) up != down
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1 test, 0 passed, 1 failed
==============================================================================
```

You fix them all in one pass instead of one run per failure.

**Check:** the run reports all the failures together.
